review: Boring and have no sense to play!
This is just an advertisement slop for the paid Battlefield 6 game. REDSEC has no real interesting game modes.

It's free, and it has some cool elements, so try it out (I'd recommend with at least one friend, coms are important)

Pros: 
- Tactical/Strategic - Large map, lots of players, tactical game that requires observation and positioning.
- Sniping - This game hits all the right notes for a sniper, the feel of sniping in this game really is top tier. 
- Destructible environment - this is by far one of the best mechanics of the game, that separates it from other BRs.
- Potential - This game has a lot of potential, however - in the BR - they need to make it competitive, unfortunately bloom, and latency issues ruin that.

Cons:
- Latency - You'll attempt to grab something from a box, it will give the animation like you succeeded, but then you realize you don't have it, and have to to turn around and press it again (hope there's not an enemy watching while you fumble with the crate)
- Bloom - This just means when you aim, your crosshair is perfectly on a stationary target, you can still miss. 
- Ping System - Try to ping something, but it won't show until a few seconds later, or it won't ping at all, the audio queue of a teammate pinging an enemy that is next to you isn't even noticeable. It makes it so that, if you don't have full team mics, the game is miserable. (Just copy Apex Legends ping system, it's the best in the genre) 
- Audio - A tank will roll up on you and you won't hear a thing.

RedSec for the first time is a really bad experience. You open a crate and it would flip upside-down, you'd try to grab a gun out of a crate, looking directly at the gun, but it would pick up the grenade next to it. Then you'd try to pick up a gun, and it just won't register, so you have to press it a few times (hope there's not an enemy looking at you at the time). The audio is terrible, a tank will roll up on you and you won't even hear it. The ping system is the worst part of the game, which is surprising, seeing as this game was made LATER than Apex Legends by years, why are we regressing? Let's add that there's bloom, which means when your crosshair is directly on your target, you will still miss randomly (Imagine - you're the last alive, everyone watching, you lock in, the enemy is in the open, you aim PERFECTLY, but you still miss, and then you die)

All-in-all: Great game that has a lot of potential, I've had a lot of fun times in RedSec when I have a team of players with mics. The strategies that we can come up with are endless. But solo queuing? It's a disaster. If you don't have at least one other person (I'd recommend a full team) then the solo experience is just, better, on other BRs. Until they fix their ping system.

​Rating: 👎 Not Recommended
Hours Played: Enough to know better
​My RTX 5070 is putting in overtime rendering Fort Lyndon in crisp 2K at 165Hz, which is genuinely fantastic because it lets me see in ultra-smooth high definition exactly how my bullets are actively avoiding the enemy.
​The weapon bloom in this game is so unhinged that if you aim center-mass at a guy 10 meters away, your gun will draw a perfect cartoon outline of bullet holes around him. You're not an elite operative; you're an abstract painter.
​Then there’s the clunky movement. Battlefield loves boasting about "Tactical Destruction" where you can blow up entire buildings, yet my highly trained soldier is completely paralyzed by the concept of a waist-high garden wall. Mantling over obstacles feels like you're trying to climb out of a swimming pool filled with wet cement.  
​Gauntlet mode is admittedly kind of cool, but the main Battle Royale experience is just looting for 15 minutes before getting instantly evaporated by an F/A-81F Super Spectre from the new Top Gun event that you couldn't even hear coming.  
​Save your SSD space. The only thing this game successfully destroyed was my patience.
